Repository evidence:
Section: What This Project Is

Self-driving is a narrowly scoped autonomous-driving repository organized around one substantial Jupyter notebook:

Camera/Lab/Visual Odometry for Localization in Autonomous Driving.ipynb

The notebook is approximately 6.1 MB, making it by far the dominant repository artifact.

localization,

That places the repository at the intersection of computer vision and robotic/autonomous localization.

The repository is therefore best understood as a focused perception/localization learning artifact rather than a general-purpose self-driving software stack.

Section: Project Scope

The checked-in tree is intentionally small:

The root README identifies the repository simply as Self-driving.

The nested path adds two useful pieces of positive context:

the work is camera-oriented,
the work is structured as a lab artifact.

The notebook title narrows that lab to visual odometry for vehicle localization.

Section: Technical Shape

The repository uses a notebook-centric workflow rather than a multi-module application architecture.

Conceptually, the artifact shape is:

This structure is useful portfolio evidence because it shows a move from earlier sensor and radar work toward camera-based vehicle localization.

Section: Jupyter Notebook Workflow

The implementation-bearing artifact is an .ipynb notebook.

That format supports an iterative workflow combining:

executable computation,

intermediate outputs,

explanatory text,

equations or narrative,

visual inspection.

The repository therefore demonstrates use of notebook-based technical exploration in a computer-vision/autonomous-systems context.

Section: Autonomous-Driving Localization

The notebook title explicitly connects visual odometry to localization in autonomous driving.

That matters because localization is a core state-estimation problem for mobile autonomous systems.

Rather than only detecting objects or simulating sensors, this repository’s focus is the vehicle’s own motion/location estimate from visual information.

That is a distinct systems concern from the radar-range and lidar-obstacle-processing work seen in immediately adjacent repositories.

Repository evidence:
Section: Overall Project Narrative

Self-driving is a compact but historically useful portfolio artifact.

It does not attempt to represent an entire autonomous-driving stack.

Instead, it isolates one important perception/localization problem and preserves it as a dedicated camera lab.

The repository demonstrates that by April 2024 the portfolio had moved beyond generic machine-learning exercises and sensor simulations into a more specialized autonomous-driving perception topic: estimating vehicle motion and localization from visual information.

Because the notebook’s internal provenance cannot be established from the repository metadata alone, the corpus keeps the personal attribution conservative while preserving the strong technical domain evidence that is directly visible.
